feature: Title text comes in by line, word or letter
summary: Any text on a video, a title's headline included, can now arrive a line, a word or a letter at a time with a stagger between pieces: rise and fade, mask reveal, blur in, track in, typewriter or wipe.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a recording, add a track above it and right click the empty track: Add Title Page > Midnight.

try.do: Type a headline into the new title page and press Command Return.
Double click the headline on the picture so its words are in hand; the panel shows a Reveal section.
Set Preset to Mask Reveal, By to Word and Stagger to 100 ms.
Press Escape twice, press Home, then step through the first second with the Right arrow.
try.shotNote: Eight real window captures, 100 ms apart, cropped to the headline and stacked. The window was behind another app, so buttons show their background look.

try.do: Press Space and watch it play.
try.shotNote: Taken with the window behind another app, so buttons show their background look.

try.do: Try Blur In by Line, then Track In and Typewriter by Letter, and Order Center Out or Random.
Export one frame at 0.4s (File, Export, PNG) and compare it with the canvas.

evaluate: Does Mask Reveal by Word read as the premium headline entrance you had in mind, or does it need a longer default length?
Is double clicking the headline an acceptable way to reach the Reveal section of a title's words?
Are Preset, By, Stagger, Each, Order and Curve the right knobs, in the right order?
Does the title's own rise on the headline fighting with the per word reveal bother you, or should picking a reveal take the part's own in off?
Should a reveal also have a way out (the words leaving a piece at a time)?
rough: The headline's own part keys (Midnight's rise and fade) still run under a reveal you add, so the whole line fades up while its words slide; a design that uses reveals on headlines is step 6 (a-set-of-titles-that-look-designed).
The mock's preset is a three way segmented control; here the six styles are a dropdown, because a list of more than three is a dropdown (UX-PATTERNS §4).
By and Order are rows the mock does not draw; the app goes further than the mock there.

The mock's closing line (One number drives the whole cascade...) moved, in the mock's words, behind the question mark on the Reveal header: it is longer than the panel's 40 character budget (UX-PATTERNS §4).
Reveals are only in (no out yet), and on a still picture with no time they do not play.
A piece rising from below can be cut at the bottom edge of the text's own box while it travels (rise and fade on the last line); mask reveal is unaffected.
Reaching a title's words takes a double click into them; the Reveal section shows while they are open, and Escape takes you back to the whole title.
